key_insight: Bayesian optimization of FSI-simulated nozzles shows a clear trade-off: rigid designs maximize impulse, while flexible designs maximize impulse delivered per unit energy.
engineering_relevance: The results guide nozzle design for pulsed-jet propulsion systems where the best choice depends on whether peak thrust or energy-efficient propulsion is the priority.
method: Compare rigid vs. flexible nozzle geometries under pulsed-jet actuation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 5× impulse amplification for rigid nozzles, about 2.5× for flexible nozzles, and a ~1.8× higher impulse-to-energy ratio for flexible designs.
watch_item: The optimized performance depends on simulation fidelity and FSI assumptions, so experimental validation is needed before translating the designs to hardware.
paper_title: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization of rigid and flexible nozzles for energy-efficient pulsed jet propulsion
